'''Ellen Louisa Burrell''' (June 12, 1850 – December 3, 1938) was an American mathematics professor, head of the Department of Pure Mathematics at [[Wellesley College]] from 1897 to 1916.

== Early life ==
Burrell was born in [[Lockport (city), New York|Lockport, New York]], the daughter of Myron Louis Burrell and Mary Jones Burrell. She earned a bachelor's degree from Wellesley College in 1880, in the same class as her future colleagues [[Katharine Lee Bates]] and [[Charlotte Fitch Roberts]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Cohen|first=Arlene|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=G_WxcNqWTAwC&dq=Ellen+Burrell+Wellesley&pg=PT28|title=Wellesley College|date=2006-05-31|publisher=Arcadia Publishing|isbn=978-1-4396-3379-3|language=en}}</ref> She went to Germany for further studies at [[University of Göttingen|Göttingen]] in 1896 and 1897.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|last=|first=|date=1938-12-05|title=Miss Ellen Burrell, Long an Educator; Ex-Head of Wellesley College Mathematics Faculty Dies|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1938/12/05/archives/miss-ellen-burrell-long-an-educator-exhead-of-wellesley-college.html|access-date=2021-10-10|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

== Career ==
Burrell taught at [[Rockford University|Rockford Seminary]] in Illinois for several years, from 1881 to 1886. She returned to Wellesley to teach in 1886.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Palmieri|first=Patricia A.|date=1983|title=Here Was Fellowship: A Social Portrait of Academic Women at Wellesley College, 1895-1920|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/368159|journal=History of Education Quarterly|volume=23|issue=2|pages=195–214|doi=10.2307/368159|jstor=368159|s2cid=144139874 |issn=0018-2680|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 1897, as a solution to her contentious relationship with fellow mathematics professor [[Ellen Hayes]], she was made head of the Department of Pure Mathematics (and Hayes became head of Applied Mathematics).<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|last=Palmieri|first=Patricia Ann|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nGgWlK9Pk1MC&dq=Ellen+Burrell+math&pg=PA326|title=In Adamless Eden: The Community of Women Faculty at Wellesley|date=1997-02-27|publisher=Yale University Press|isbn=978-0-300-06388-2|pages=128-129; 326, n. 67|language=en}}</ref> Her department included professors [[Roxana Vivian]] and [[Helen Abbot Merrill|Helen Abbott Merrill]].<ref>Wellesley College, ''[https://repository.wellesley.edu/object/wellesley627 Legenda]'' (1915 yearbook): 34.</ref> She and Hayes both retired from Wellesley in 1916, and the departments were reunited.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Green|first1=Judy|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IRbOAwAAQBAJ&dq=Burrell+Wellesley&pg=PA23|title=Pioneering Women in American Mathematics: The Pre-1940 PhD's|last2=LaDuke|first2=Jeanne|date=2009|publisher=American Mathematical Soc.|isbn=978-0-8218-4376-5|pages=23|language=en}}</ref> She was also curator of the college's herbarium.<ref name=":0" /> Her class notes were privately published as "The Number System" and "Synthetic Projection Geometry".<ref name=":1" />

Burrell attended the fourth colloquium of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in Boston in 1903,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Cole|first=F. N.|date=December 1903|title=The Boston Colloquium of the American Mathematical Society|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1903-10-03/S0002-9904-1903-01074-X/S0002-9904-1903-01074-X.pdf|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|volume=10|issue=3|pages=119–120|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1903-01074-X}}</ref> and another 1903 meeting of the society held at [[Columbia University]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Cole|first=F. N.|date=1903-03-20|title=American Mathematical Society|url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.17.429.468-a|journal=Science|language=en|volume=17|issue=429|pages=468|doi=10.1126/science.17.429.468-a|issn=0036-8075}}</ref> She was also active in the Association of Mathematics Teachers of New England.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Francis|first=William A.|date=February 1907|title=Association of Mathematics Teachers of New England|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kAEUAAAAIAAJ&dq=Ellen+Burrell+Wellesley&pg=PA153|journal=School Science and Mathematics|volume=7|pages=153}}</ref> She visited the American School for Girls in Constantinople in 1907.<ref>{{Cite news|date=1907-10-17|title=The American College|pages=14|work=Boston Evening Transcript|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/86845198/the-american-college/|access-date=2021-10-10|via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Burrell enthusiastically voted for [[Warren G. Harding]] for president in 1920.<ref>{{Cite book|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8MsgAAAAMAAJ&dq=Ellen+L.+Burrell+Wellesley&pg=PA124|title=The Wellesley Alumnae Quarterly|date=January 1921|publisher=Wellesley College Alumnae Association|pages=125|language=en|chapter=Alumnae Notes}}</ref> She died in 1938, aged 88 years, in Roxbury, Massachusetts.<ref name=":0" /> Her papers are in the Wellesley College Archives.<ref name=":1" />
